We lost the time our best DPS accidentally deleted their own character’s inventory and we had to spend an hour helping them rebuild it from a screenshot they took three weeks earlier, which was missing half the items because they had been "organizing." We lost the argument about whether the guild name should have a space in it, which went on for so long that by the time we decided, the name was already taken by a guild that had been playing for two years and had no idea we were having an existential crisis about typography.

But here is the thing about losses, and I think this is the thing that makes this guild different from the ones that just grind and grind and never really connect: we do not let the losses define us. We let them teach us. We let them make us funnier, and sharper, and a little more suspicious of anyone who says "this is easy" without having actually done it. Every wipe, every failed quest, every time we got our asses handed to us by a boss that was clearly designed by someone who had a personal grudge against our class composition, we took it, we laughed about it, and we came back the next day with a slightly better plan and a slightly bigger grudge.
